Struer is a Danish municipality assessed in the Annual Report from the Database for Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark, which covers the period from 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2023 and is published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) [^src1]. The report evaluates the clinical quality of atrial fibrillation treatment across all 98 Danish municipalities, emphasizing decentralized quality development and local benchmarking within the Danish healthcare system [^src2].

Regarding Indicator 4b, which measures adherence to safety practices when using DOAC (Direct Oral Anticoagulant) medications, Struer demonstrated strong performance [^src1]. The municipality achieved a compliance rate of 95.4%, successfully meeting the criteria for 434 out of 455 relevant patients [^src1]. This result is significant because it places Struer among the municipalities that meet and exceed the national standard requirement of ≥95% [^src1]. 

Struer is also evaluated under other clinical indicators detailed in the latter sections of the report, such as early initiation of anticoagulation therapy (Indicator 1) and stroke prevention (Indicator 5) [^src2]. In these additional metrics, Struer recorded figures of 5 out of 614 (0.8%) and 10 out of 599 (1.7%), reflecting its broader statistical profile in the national database [^src2]. While the available data primarily consists of statistical benchmarking rows without extensive narrative claims, it firmly establishes Struer's role in the national quality assurance framework for atrial fibrillation care.
